header.userPrompt:
# Make the idempotent "get-or-create" write paths race-safe

## Problem

Several write paths are *idempotent by intent* — "return the existing row, or
create it", or "create it unless an equivalent one already exists (then do
nothing)". They are currently implemented as check-then-write: read by the
natural key, then insert when the read found nothing.

Under concurrency this races: two requests both read "absent" and both insert.
The second insert hits the unique constraint and surfaces as an unhandled
`PSQLException` / generic 500 — even though the *intended* behaviour is simply
to converge on the one existing row (or skip), never to error.

This is the idempotent counterpart to the reject-on-conflict work already
merged (PR #53): there, a genuine duplicate must become a clean domain error;
here, a "duplicate" is the normal, expected outcome and must be absorbed, not
reported.

## Sites to fix

1. **Category get-or-create.** `CreateCategoryAction` looks up a category by
   name and returns it if present, else creates it. The two Telegram
   `findOrCreateCategory` helpers (`TelegramExpenseAction`,
   `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction`) do the same thing independently. All
   three must become race-safe and should share one path. Backing constraint:
   `category_user_id_name_unique (user_id, name)`.

2. **Pending-merchant get-or-create.** `MerchantsRepository.createPendingIfAbsent`
   (used by receipt parsing and the Telegram expense flow) looks up a merchant
   by name, returns its id if present, else inserts a pending merchant and
   returns the new id. Backing constraint: `merchant_user_id_name_unique
   (user_id, name)`.

3. **Auto `set_merchant` rule create-if-absent.** Three callers learn a
   `set_merchant` import rule from a confirmed/parsed receipt or a
   duplicate-merchant merge — `ConfirmReceiptAction`, `ParseReceiptAction`,
   `MarkMerchantAsDuplicateAction`. Each currently calls
   `ImportRuleRepository.existsByUserPatternMerchant` and only creates the rule
   when it returns false. The intent is "create this rule if an equivalent one
   isn't already there, otherwise leave the existing one untouched". Backing
   constraint: the partial unique index `merchant_rule_set_merchant_unique
   (user_id, pattern, merchant_id) WHERE action = 'set_merchant'`.

4. **Upload dedup.** `UploadDocumentAction` + `DocumentsRepository.create`
   store a document keyed by `(user_id, sha256)` and enqueue a `ProcessDocument`
   background job. Re-uploading the same file must return the *existing*
   document's id and must NOT enqueue a second processing job. Today the dedup
   relies on an upfront `findBySha256`; a concurrent first-time upload of the
   same bytes races into the unique violation. Backing constraint:
   `document_user_sha256_unique (user_id, sha256)`.

## Requirements / acceptance criteria

- No observable behaviour change on the happy path: get-or-create returns the
  existing row when the natural key already exists and the newly-created row
  otherwise; create-if-absent is a no-op when an equivalent row exists; upload
  dedup returns the existing document id and enqueues no extra job.
- Two concurrent calls with the same natural key must converge on exactly one
  row and neither must fail with a 500 / unhandled DB exception.
- The uniqueness guarantee must come from the existing DB constraint, not from
  an application-level read that "looks free then inserts". A pre-read may
  remain only as a genuine advisory fast path (e.g. skipping the S3 re-upload in
  the upload flow) — never as the thing that guarantees correctness.
- Tenant/ownership already enforced at the write (e.g. the referenced merchant
  of a rule must belong to the user) must stay enforced.
- Tests must assert idempotency directly: calling the path twice yields the
  same id and a single row; the auto-rule path twice leaves one rule.

## Conventions (already codified in `.orca/reviewers/`)

- Correctness invariants live at the database, not in a check-then-write
  (`coding-patterns.md`).
- Conflict handling belongs at the repository boundary; catching a
  `PSQLException`/`SQLException` there for this purpose is expected
  (`persistence.md`). Note the distinction: that reviewer describes
  *translating* a conflict into a domain error for reject semantics. These
  sites are the opposite — the conflict must be *absorbed* (converge / skip),
  not turned into an error.
- `TextractCacheDAO.create` already shows the idiom in this codebase:
  `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (…) DO NOTHING`. Choose whatever fits each site best
  (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING [RETURNING …]` or a targeted catch-to-absorb); the
  reviewers do not mandate one mechanism, only that the DB constraint is the
  guarantee.
- One new Play evolution per PR max; these fixes should need **no** schema
  change — every backing constraint listed above already exists.

## Out of scope (do NOT touch — separate follow-ups)

- `CreateBankStatementDraftAction` reject-path pre-checks (the "already in your
  import queue" check has no backing constraint and is intentionally left as an
  advisory UX guard; the other two are reject-translate, not get-or-create).
- Row→refund / row→expense double-link guards in `CreateRefundFromRowAction` /
  `CreateExpenseFromRowAction` (no unique constraint; needs a conditional
  update, a different pattern).
- Moving refund/expense referenced-entity ownership checks into their
  repositories.

resultJson.description:
Four server write paths are meant to be idempotent: category get-or-create, pending-merchant get-or-create, auto-learned `set_merchant` import rules, and upload dedup by `(user_id, sha256)`. Today each one reads by the natural key and inserts only if the read found nothing. If two requests run at once, both can see "absent", both insert, and the second one hits a unique constraint and fails as an unhandled `PSQLException` (a 500). For these paths, finding a duplicate is the normal case. The duplicate should be absorbed: return the one existing row, or do nothing. It should not be reported as an error.

The fix makes the existing DB constraint the guarantee at the repository boundary. Each site gets an atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (<constraint columns>) DO NOTHING [RETURNING id]`, following the existing `TextractCacheDAO.create` idiom. When the insert returns nothing, the same transaction reads the winning row by the natural key. Under READ COMMITTED, ON CONFLICT waits for the competing transaction to commit, so the follow-up SELECT sees the row. Ownership checks that run inside the write transaction stay where they are: the `set_merchant` rule's merchant must belong to the user. A pre-read can stay only as an advisory fast path, such as skipping the S3 put on re-upload. No schema change or evolution is needed, because every backing constraint already exists in `evolutions/default/3.sql`.

On the happy path nothing visible changes. Get-or-create returns the existing row (the stored name, matched case-insensitively) or the newly created one. Create-if-absent does nothing when an equivalent row exists. Re-uploading returns the existing document id and enqueues no second `ProcessDocument` job. Tests check idempotency directly: two calls give the same id and one row. Repository specs also fire several calls in parallel, which pass under any interleaving because the DB serialises them. Reject-on-conflict paths (PR #53, `ConstraintViolations.translating`) are not touched.

tasks.title: Race-safe category get-or-create shared by CreateCategoryAction and both Telegram flows
tasks.description: Add `CategoryDAO.createIfAbsent(request: Category.Create)(implicit conn): Option[UUID]`: `INSERT INTO category … ON CONFLICT (user_id, name) DO NOTHING RETURNING id`, parsed with `SqlParser.scalar[UUID].singleOpt`. Add `CategoriesRepository.getOrCreate(userId: UUID, name: String): Future[Category]`. In one `withTransaction`, it builds a `Category.Create` (id `UuidCreator.getTimeOrderedEpoch()`, now from the injected `clock`), calls `createIfAbsent`, and on `None` returns `CategoryDAO.findByName(userId, name)`; if that row has meanwhile vanished, it throws `RuntimeException("Category not found")`. On `Some(id)` it returns the created row (re-read with `CategoryDAO.find(id, userId)` or build it from the Create). Do not wrap the new method in `ConstraintViolations.translating`; the conflict is absorbed. Switch `CreateCategoryAction.apply` to `validateFormat`, then `getOrCreate`, mapping to `CreateCategory.Response(id, name)`. It must keep returning the stored row's name on a hit, so drop its chimney/UuidCreator/Clock usage if it becomes unused. Replace the private `findOrCreateCategory` in `TelegramExpenseAction` and in `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction` with `categoriesRepository.getOrCreate(userId, name).map(_.id)`, and remove the now-unused `Category`/`UuidCreator` imports. `CategoriesRepository.findByName` is then unused in main code: remove it and its two `"findByName"` spec cases in `CategoriesRepositorySpec` (the DAO's `findByName` stays). Tests in `CategoriesRepositorySpec`, under a `"getOrCreate"` should-block: creates when absent; returns the existing id and stored name for a case-variant name with one row in `all`; two sequential calls give the same id and one row; N parallel calls (`Future.sequence`) all succeed with one distinct id and one row; same name for two users gives two rows. In `CategoriesControllerSpec`, POST the same name twice and get the same id. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *CategoriesRepositorySpec *CategoriesControllerSpec *TelegramExpenseActionSpec *UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseActionSpec"`.

tasks.title: Race-safe MerchantsRepository.createPendingIfAbsent
tasks.description: Add `MerchantDAO.createIfAbsent(request: Merchant.Create)(implicit conn): Option[UUID]`: the same INSERT as `MerchantDAO.create` plus `ON CONFLICT (user_id, name) DO NOTHING RETURNING id`. Use an explicit conflict target so a `merchant_tax_id_user_idx` conflict is never silently swallowed (pending merchants have taxId None anyway). Rewrite `MerchantsRepository.createPendingIfAbsent(userId, name): Future[UUID]` (signature unchanged) inside `withTransaction`: build the pending `Merchant.Create` (reviewed=false, notes/category/taxId None), `createIfAbsent`, and on `None` fall back to `MerchantDAO.findByName(userId, name).map(_.id)`, throwing `RuntimeException("Merchant not found")` if it is absent. The upfront `findByName` check-then-insert goes away. Callers (`ParseReceiptAction`, `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction`) need no change. Add a `"createPendingIfAbsent"` block to `MerchantsRepositorySpec`: creates a pending (reviewed=false) merchant when absent; returns the existing id for an existing (case-variant) name without changing that merchant's reviewed flag; two sequential calls give the same id and one row (`merchants.all`); N parallel calls all succeed with one distinct id and one row; per-user isolation. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *MerchantsRepositorySpec *MerchantReviewControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Race-safe auto set_merchant rule create-if-absent
tasks.description: Add `ImportRuleDAO.createSetMerchantIfAbsent(rule: ImportRule.Create)(implicit conn): Unit` with the same INSERT as `create` plus `ON CONFLICT (user_id, pattern, merchant_id) WHERE action = 'set_merchant' DO NOTHING`. The WHERE predicate is required so Postgres can infer the partial unique index `merchant_rule_set_merchant_unique`. Add `ImportRuleRepository.createSetMerchantIfAbsent(userId: UUID, merchantId: UUID, pattern: String): Future[Unit]`. In one `withTransaction`, it calls the existing private `verifyReferencesOwned(ImportRuleAction.SetMerchant(merchantId), userId)`, which keeps the ownership check at the write and throws "Merchant not found". It then builds `ImportRule.Create(autoCreated = true, …)` and calls the DAO method. Do not wrap it in `ConstraintViolations.translating`. Replace the exists-then-create blocks in `ConfirmReceiptAction` (the `(Some(parsedName), Some(mId))` branch), `ParseReceiptAction` (~line 104, inside `createPendingIfAbsent(...).flatMap`), and `MarkMerchantAsDuplicateAction` (before `rePointAndDelete`; keep that order) with a single call to the new method. `existsByUserPatternMerchant` then has no main-code callers, so delete it from the repository and the DAO, along with its comment and the `"existsByUserPatternMerchant"` block in `ImportRuleRepositorySpec`. In `ParseReceiptActionSpec` (~lines 372-376 and 436-440), replace the `existsByUserPatternMerchant`/`create` stubs with `when(ruleRepo.createSetMerchantIfAbsent(any(), any(), anyString())).thenReturn(Future.unit)`. Unstubbed Mockito methods return a null Future and would NPE. Tests in `ImportRuleRepositorySpec` under `"createSetMerchantIfAbsent"`: creates one auto_created set_merchant rule; a second call (also a case-variant pattern) leaves exactly one rule for that user/pattern/merchant; N parallel calls succeed and leave one rule; it fails with "Merchant not found" for another user's merchant and creates no rule; an existing manual rule (autoCreated=false) stays untouched (same id, autoCreated still false). Run `rg existsByUserPatternMerchant` to confirm no references remain. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *ImportRuleRepositorySpec *ParseReceiptActionSpec *ReceiptsControllerSpec *MerchantReviewControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Race-safe upload dedup in DocumentsRepository.create / UploadDocumentAction
tasks.description: Add `DocumentDAO.createIfAbsent(request: Document.Create)(implicit conn): Option[UUID]`: the same INSERT as `DocumentDAO.create` plus `ON CONFLICT (user_id, sha256) DO NOTHING RETURNING id`. Leave `DocumentDAO.create` as is; `ReceiptRepository` and `BankStatementDraftRepository` still use it and are out of scope. Change `DocumentsRepository.create(document, job)` to return `Future[UUID]`, the id of the stored document. In one `withTransaction`, `createIfAbsent(document)`: on `Some(id)` insert the job with `BackgroundJobDAO.create(job)` and return id; on `None` return `DocumentDAO.findBySha256(document.userId, document.sha256)`'s id without inserting the job (throw `RuntimeException("Document not found")` if it is absent). In `UploadDocumentAction`, keep the upfront `findBySha256` as an advisory fast path that skips the S3 `exists`/`put`, and add a comment saying it is not the dedup guarantee. On the create path, respond with the id returned by `documentsRepository.create`, not the locally generated `documentId`. Existing callers that discard the result (`RepositoryUtils.createDocument` line ~406, `DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec.makeDocument`) keep compiling. Tests in `DocumentsRepositorySpec` under `"create"`: a second create with the same (user, sha256) but a different doc id returns the first id, leaves one document row, and leaves exactly one ProcessDocument job for that document. Count jobs with a read-only query via `repositories.database.withConnection`, for example `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM background_jobs WHERE payload ...`; check the actual table/column names in the evolutions and `BackgroundJobDAO`. Add N parallel creates with the same sha → one distinct id, one document, one job, plus per-user isolation. Make sure each test uses a random sha (`RandomData.randomString`), because the Postgres container is shared. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *DocumentsRepositorySpec *DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec *DocumentsControllerSpec"` (the S3 spec needs Docker).

resultJson.brief:
Modules: `server/` (Play backend; controllers → actions in `net/wiringbits/actions/**` → repositories in `net/wiringbits/repositories/*Repository.scala` → Anorm DAOs in `repositories/daos/*DAO.scala`). Schema: `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/3.sql` (squashed). Do NOT add an evolution.

Backing constraints (all in 3.sql):
- `category`: `name CITEXT`, `CONSTRAINT category_user_id_name_unique UNIQUE (user_id, name)`.
- `merchant`: `name CITEXT`, `CONSTRAINT merchant_user_id_name_unique UNIQUE (user_id, name)`. Separately there is a partial unique index `merchant_tax_id_user_idx (user_id, tax_id) WHERE tax_id IS NOT NULL`, so always give ON CONFLICT an explicit target.
- `merchant_rule`: `pattern CITEXT`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX merchant_rule_set_merchant_unique ON merchant_rule (user_id, pattern, merchant_id) WHERE action = 'set_merchant'`. For ON CONFLICT on a partial index you must repeat the predicate: `ON CONFLICT (user_id, pattern, merchant_id) WHERE action = 'set_merchant' DO NOTHING`.
- `document`: `CONSTRAINT document_user_sha256_unique UNIQUE (user_id, sha256)`.
Because the columns are CITEXT, conflicts are case-insensitive; DAO `findByName` queries use `name = $name::CITEXT`.

Idiom to copy: `TextractCacheDAO.create` (`daos/TextractCacheDAO.scala`) uses `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (sha256, api_type) DO NOTHING`. Anorm style: `import anorm.*`; interpolated `SQL"""…"""`; UUIDs passed as `${id.toString}::UUID`; Option UUIDs as `${opt.map(_.toString)}::UUID`. Read a returned id with `.as(anorm.SqlParser.scalar[UUID].singleOpt)` (used in `MerchantDAO.findAndDeletePending`). Writes that return Unit use `val _ = SQL"…".executeUpdate()`.

Get-or-create pattern: inside `database.withTransaction { implicit conn => … }`, run `insert … ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING RETURNING id`. On `None`, read the existing row by natural key in the same transaction. Postgres is READ COMMITTED, so ON CONFLICT blocks until the competing insert commits and the next statement's snapshot sees it. Missing data must fail loudly (throw `RuntimeException("<Entity> not found")`), never fabricate. Do NOT wrap these absorb-paths in `ConstraintViolations.translating` (`repositories/ConstraintViolations.scala`); that helper is for reject semantics (it maps a PSQLException message containing a constraint name to a `RuntimeException(message)`) and stays on the existing `create`/`update` methods.

Repository conventions: classes are `@Inject() (database: Database)(implicit ec: DatabaseExecutionContext, clock: Clock)`. Methods are `Future { database.withTransaction/withConnection { implicit conn => … } }`. Ids come from `UuidCreator.getTimeOrderedEpoch()` (com.github.f4b6a3.uuid) and timestamps from `clock.instant()`. Tenant checks run inside the write transaction. `ImportRuleRepository` has `private def verifyReferencesOwned(action: ImportRuleAction, userId: UUID)(implicit conn: Connection): Unit`, which throws "Merchant not found"/"Category not found".

Key current code:
- `CategoriesRepository.create(Category.Create): Future[Unit]`, `findByName(userId, name): Future[Option[Category]]`. `Category.Create(id, userId, name, createdAt, updatedAt)`. `CategoryDAO.{create, find(id,userId), findByName(userId,name)}`.
- `CreateCategoryAction.apply(userId, CreateCategory.Request): Future[CreateCategory.Response(id, name)]` has a `validateFormat` (blank / >25 chars). Its only caller is `controllers/CategoriesController.scala`.
- Telegram duplicates: `actions/telegram/TelegramExpenseAction.scala:129` and `actions/telegram/UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.scala:94`, both `private def findOrCreateCategory(userId, name): Future[UUID]`.
- `MerchantsRepository.createPendingIfAbsent(userId: UUID, name: String): Future[UUID]` (`repositories/MerchantsRepository.scala:38`). `Merchant.Create(id, userId, name, notes, categoryId, taxId, reviewed, createdAt, updatedAt)`. `MerchantDAO.{create, findByName}`. `MerchantsRepository.findByName` is still used by TelegramExpenseAction, so keep it.
- `ImportRuleRepository.create(userId, action: ImportRuleAction, pattern, autoCreated = false): Future[UUID]` and `existsByUserPatternMerchant(userId, pattern, merchantId, excludeId: Option[UUID] = None): Future[Boolean]`. Only three main callers use the latter, all without excludeId: `actions/receipts/ConfirmReceiptAction.scala:76`, `actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala:104`, `actions/merchants/MarkMerchantAsDuplicateAction.scala:28`. `ImportRule.Create(id, userId, action, pattern, autoCreated, createdAt, updatedAt)`. `ImportRuleAction.SetMerchant(merchantId)` lives in `lib/api/shared` (`net.wiringbits.api.models.merchants.ImportRuleAction`) and has `entryName`, `merchantIdOpt`, `categoryIdOpt`.
- `DocumentsRepository.create(document: Document.Create, job: BackgroundJobData.Create): Future[Unit]` inserts document + job atomically; `findBySha256(userId, sha256): Future[Option[Document]]`. `DocumentDAO.create` is also called by `ReceiptRepository` and `BankStatementDraftRepository` (leave those alone). `UploadDocumentAction` (`actions/documents/UploadDocumentAction.scala`) does findBySha256 → (S3 `blobStorage.exists`/`put` at key `data/$userId/$date/$sha256`) → create, and returns `UploadDocument.Response(id)`. Other findBySha256 users (UploadReceiptAction, TelegramPhotoAction, CreateBankStatementDraftAction) are out of scope.
- `BackgroundJobsRepository` has no read/count method; for test assertions use a read-only SQL through `repositories.database.withConnection` (look up the table/columns in evolutions/`BackgroundJobDAO`).

Out of scope (do not touch): CreateBankStatementDraftAction pre-checks; the row→refund/expense double-link guards; moving refund/expense ownership checks; UploadReceiptAction/ReceiptRepository dedup.

Testing (docs/guide/testing.md): repository specs extend `net.wiringbits.core.RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils`, use `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => … }`, `repositories.<categories|merchants|importRules|documents|database>`, and the factories `createUser()`, `createCategory(userId, name)`, `createMerchant(userId, name, …)`, `createImportRule(userId, pattern, action: ImportRuleActionKind, merchantId, categoryId)`, `createDocument(userId, sha256, …)` from `server/src/test/scala/utils/RepositoryUtils.scala`. Never seed with raw SQL; read-only assertion queries are OK. The Postgres testcontainer is shared across the JVM, so use random/user-scoped values and user-scoped assertions. Should-subjects are method names only (e.g. `"getOrCreate" should { "return the existing id …" in … }`), never the class name. Use `.futureValue`; for failures use the spec-local `expectError` helper or `intercept[RuntimeException](…futureValue)` (the message is in `getCause.getMessage`). For concurrency tests, fire N calls (e.g. 8) with `Future.sequence` and assert all succeed, `distinct.size == 1`, and one row. These pass under any interleaving, so they are not flaky. Actions are mostly covered via controller specs (`controllers/*ControllerSpec.scala`, PlayPostgresSpec + mocked external boundaries). Mockito-based action specs (`ParseReceiptActionSpec`, `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseActionSpec`) must stub every repo method the action calls, because unstubbed methods return null Futures. `TelegramExpenseActionSpec` uses real repos.

Build: compile with `-Werror` via `CI=true sbt Test/compile`; unused imports fail the build, so remove the imports your change orphans. Run only targeted specs: `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"`. Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`. Do not run the full `sbt test`. Known flake: BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec "allowed errors" under full parallel runs. Comment density is low; keep only short intent comments (e.g. why the pre-read is advisory).

findings.title: Unrelated yarn.lock rewrites still in the change set

reason.text: Already fixed in the working tree, so this is environmental. lib/ui/yarn.lock and web/yarn.lock are reverted to 086ffcf and staged, and `git diff 086ffcf -- lib/ui/yarn.lock web/yarn.lock` is empty. HEAD is still 33a7ac4 because the runtime makes the commits and I'm not allowed to commit. The reviewer is reading the commit stat rather than the working tree. There is nothing left to change in the codebase.

entries.resultJson:
The full suite passes: `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` exited with code 0, so nothing needed fixing.

- **Results:** every module reported "All tests passed". The server module ran 859 tests and the others ran 36, 56 and 244, with no failures.
- **Setup:** I used Node v24.15.0 because the default v16 rejects `--openssl-legacy-provider`. Docker was already running, so the testcontainers Postgres started by itself.
- **Commit state:** the test run didn't change any tracked files. The flow has committed the earlier work as `6899e68`. That commit includes the new upload race test and puts both `yarn.lock` files back to their base (`086ffcf`) versions.
